With the slogan “Recycling Starts With You,” a Packaging Collection Competition started on 23 December 2024 and ended on 27 March 2025. The competition was held in 3 categories: Children, Adult 1, and Adult 2. A total of 319 people participated, and a total of 37 tons (37,054 kg) of waste was recovered for recycling. The Awards Ceremony of the “Recycling Starts With You” Competition, organized by Çanakkale Municipality's Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste, ÇAKAB (Çanakkale Solid Waste Management Union), and Veolia Çanakkale Waste Services Inc., was held on 14 April 2025 in order to increase awareness about the correct and separate collection of packaging waste.

At the level of Çanakkale province, in order to strengthen and sustain relationships and cooperation between civil society and local government (public sector); to increase awareness and knowledge of stakeholders and the public about global, national, and local strategies, treaties, policies, and practices in the fields of climate change and sustainability; and to enable, strengthen, and sustain civil society-citizen participation in the implementation and monitoring of climate change-related policies (Climate Action Plan) in Çanakkale, the project “A Participatory and Inclusive Climate Action Model: Çanakkale Climate Action Group and Climate Ambassadors,” supported by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and jointly implemented by the Turkey Europe Foundation and our Municipality's Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste, held its Opening Event on 26 February 2025. Within the scope of the project, a Municipal Units Coordination Meeting was held on 22 April 2025 to discuss the Climate Action Plan, allocate responsibilities before the external stakeholders meetings. In working groups on Water Management, Climate Adaptation and Awareness, Energy and Transportation, the opinions and recommendations of participants were evaluated, and interactive discussions were held about shaping climate policies together in Çanakkale, as well as ideas regarding possible works that could be carried out under the project, in Information and Consultation Meetings with municipal departments and external stakeholders on 21, 22, and 27 May. On 17 June, a “Climate Ambassadors and Climate Action Group Workshop” was held to discuss the prominent ideas raised in working groups under Water Management, Climate Adaptation & Awareness, Energy, and Transportation, with the aim of shaping our city's climate policies together. On 24-25 June, within the scope of the project, a working visit was carried out to Kadıköy Municipality by a project group of 10 people, consisting of a member of our Municipal Council, employees of the Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste, City Volunteers, and representatives of civil society organizations, to strengthen existing cooperation, exchange knowledge mutually, and examine successful environmental projects on site.

Çanakkale Municipality's Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste has designed and distributed the 2025 waste calendar in cooperation with ÇAKAB and Veolia.

The works for once again flying the internationally standard environmental Blue Flag at Barış Beach, Güzelyalı, and Dardanos Municipal Public Beach this season have been completed by the Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste, and the Season Opening took place with the Blue Flag Ceremony at Dardanos Municipal Public Beach on Monday, 23 June 2025, at 10:00 AM.

Studies continue regarding the Zero Waste Park that will be carried out in cooperation with the Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste, the Directorate of Parks & Gardens, and the Directorate of Public Works.

Within the scope of awareness training in Climate Change and Zero Waste, between January and the end of June, a total of 16 training sessions were given, reaching 729 people.

For verification of used vegetable oil agreements of businesses, a total of 160 workplaces were inspected in cooperation with the Directorate of Climate Change and Zero Waste and the Directorate of Municipal Police (Zabıta), and this work was completed on 5 May 2025.

On 29 May, as part of World Environment Day events, between 30 May and 1 June, for citizens who come with their own cups and who help reduce use-and-throw materials, a 40% discount was applied at the machine‐coffees in our municipality's 5 social facilities (Golf Family Tea Garden, Freedom Park, Peace Café, Türkan Saylan Social Facilities, Güzelyalı Public Beach). The project was realized, and shared via our municipality's social media accounts.

As part of the Zero Waste efforts under the EKAY framework, together with the Beneficiary (“Hak Sahibi”), ÇAKAB prepared a report “Pilot Application and Models for Container Placement within Zero Waste Practices.” Within the boundaries of Çanakkale Municipality, in Esenler Neighborhood's pilot application, a joint study by the Union (ÇAKAB), the Beneficiary, and municipal teams was conducted to optimize waste collection processes in 954 independent units across 49 buildings, and the Union prepared the “Directive on Procedures and Principles for Dual Waste Collection Systems for Mass Housing and Site Settlements.”

On 11 April 2025, teams from the Directorate of Cleaning Works together with students of the Food Engineering Department of Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University carried out cleaning work on the Güzelyalı, Dardanos, and Yeni Kordon beaches.

On 16 April 2025, a “Çanakkale Province Vector Control Seminar” was organized in cooperation with the Faculty of Agriculture of Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University, the Environmental Health Unit of the Provincial Health Directorate, and a biologist expert, where the situation of biocidal product applications for vector control in Çanakkale was discussed.

On 22 April 2025, a briefing meeting on waste management was held for tradespeople in our city's “Çarşı” (Marketplace) district by our Municipality's Cleaning Works Directorate.

As part of our annual work concerning mosquitoes remaining from previous years, “Wintering Cycle Control” works have been launched by our Cleaning Works Directorate. In this effort, once, using the “Hot Fogging” method, biocidal product applicator personnel worked to disable possible mosquitoes in underground rainwater and sewer lines in the city. Afterwards, larval control has been implemented in wetlands and water accumulations in the city, and insecticide activities (spraying) in open areas are being carried out with ULV (Ultra-Low Volume) application throughout all streets and avenues within our municipality and its surrounding area. Also, trash containers—which serve as breeding places for houseflies—are regularly washed and treated. In the central area of Çanakkale (including Güzelyalı and Dardanos), covering 3,589 hectares (1899 ha for central area + Güzelyalı and Dardanos), regular spraying is carried out.

On 31 May 2025, together with Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart University and the Provincial Health Directorate, at Peace Promenade Beach (“Barış Kordonu”), as part of the “Don't Toss Your Butts, Sow Seeds” event, cigarette butt collection and seed card distribution was carried out.

On 3 June, as part of Marmara Sea Day events, Çanakkale Municipality, ÇOMÜ Maritime Sciences and Technology, held an awareness event including seabed cleanup and a photography exhibition addressing marine pollution.

In the suburban areas of Güzelyalı and Dardanos within our municipality, wastewater generated is treated at the Güzelyalı Dardanos Advanced Biological Wastewater Treatment Plant, and the treated water will be used in green areas of the region by integrating reuse units into the facility. Currently in permit processes, once completed, the facility's discharge water will be diverted to reuse units and used as an alternative for green field irrigation via the “Purple Network.”

Wastewater in the Güzelyalı and Dardanos suburban areas is treated in the Advanced Biological Wastewater Treatment Plant designed with I-FAS (Integrated Fixed-film Activated Sludge) process. Our plant, being among the first of its kind in Turkey for this process, has capacity of 3,750 m³/day in the first stage and 5,000 m³/day in the second stage. Thanks to the advantages of the I-FAS system, treatment is efficient even under large flows in relatively compact space.

Sludges arising from wastewater treatment plants are dried at our Solar Sludge Drying Facility within our central plant and turned into usable material. When the treatment plant was initially commissioned, dewatering was the terminal step. The treatment sludge, which had 20% dryness, is brought up to 90% dryness at the Solar Sludge Drying Plant. No additional heat source is used; the sludge is dried by the sun.

Beside the Central Advanced Biological Wastewater Treatment Plant of Çanakkale Municipality, there is a Solar Power Plant covering 14,550 square meters. In this solar field, there are 3,828 locally produced panels of 280 watts capacity each. Çanakkale Municipality has solved part of its energy needs through this environmental investment. The solar field helps treat wastewater, and the sludge in the solar drying facility is also dried with solar power. Thanks to this cycle we have gained Blue Flag beaches, an important eco-label. Beşiktaş Municipality has been strengthening its climate action agenda through the Sustainable Energy and Climate Action Plan (SECAP) and related strategic initiatives. Building on the ambitious greenhouse gas (GHG) reduction targets set in 2024, the municipality has transitioned from a predominantly planning phase in previous years to a progressive implementation phase in 2024-2025.

Key Developments and Achievements (2024-2025):

Renewable Energy Integration: Preparatory feasibility studies and pilot projects for solar photovoltaic systems on public buildings have been completed. In addition, preliminary steps have been taken for renewable energy applications in residential and tertiary buildings, with technical assessments guiding the scaling up of solar capacity by 2030.

Electrification of the Municipal Fleet: Initial procurement processes for electric vehicles (EVs) within the municipal fleet have been initiated, with associated EV charging infrastructure planning under development. These steps represent a shift from strategic commitment to concrete operationalization.

Waste Management and Circular Economy: Implementation of the national Zero Waste Program continues at the municipal level, reinforced by the official Zero Waste Certificate. New awareness-raising campaigns accompany operational improvements in recycling and organic waste management, contributing to reduced methane emissions and increased alignment with circular economy principles.

Community Education and Engagement: Beyond infrastructural projects, the municipality has focused on awareness programs for younger generations. In 2024-2025, workshops, trainings, and educational activities have been organized with middle school students and local communities, embedding environmental literacy and climate awareness at the grassroots level. These activities are designed to build long-term resilience by fostering behavioral change and civic participation.

Environmental Standards and Recognition: Beşiktaş Municipality has achieved internationally recognized certifications, including the ISO 14001:2015 Environmental Management System Certificate, validating its structured approach to environmental governance. In addition, the municipality has maintained its Carbon Neutral Certificates (2019 and 2020), confirming ongoing commitments to offsetting carbon emissions, and continues to hold the Zero Waste Certificate, further underscoring its leadership in sustainable practices.

Strategic and Financial Dimension:
One of the significant advancements since 2024 has been the integration of climate-related actions and costs into the official Strategic Plan of Beşiktaş Municipality. Each climate-relevant objective and activity is now linked with a financial estimate, providing a clear roadmap for implementation. This allows the municipality not only to demonstrate ambition but also to track and justify the required resources. While financial constraints persist, this institutionalization of cost planning strengthens Beşiktaş's capacity to apply for external funding. The municipality actively explores innovative financing models, including public-private partnerships, national programs, regional funds, and international climate finance mechanisms (e.g., ODA and green funds).

Global Context and Alignment:
Beşiktaş Municipality's climate action efforts remain aligned with both national climate strategies and international frameworks. In addition to the Paris Agreement, Beşiktaş explicitly links its actions with the European Green Deal and the Covenant of Mayors, demonstrating its role as a local authority integrated into global climate governance. These alignments are critical in ensuring that municipal-level achievements contribute to Turkey's overall commitments and global sustainability pathways.

Overall Impact:
Beşiktaş Municipality's dual focus on mitigation and adaptation ensures that while emissions are being reduced through renewable energy, electrification, and efficiency measures, the community is also being prepared for climate impacts through infrastructure upgrades, awareness campaigns, and resilience planning. The municipality's strategic location within Istanbul, as a cultural, economic, and demographic hub, magnifies the impact of its actions. Each successful initiative not only benefits Beşiktaş residents but also provides a replicable model for other urban areas across Turkey and internationally.

Conclusion:
The reporting year marks a shift for Beşiktaş from “commitment and planning” to “early implementation and institutional strengthening.” Through the combination of new certifications, pilot projects, awareness-raising programs, and the integration of costs into strategic planning, the municipality has established a stronger foundation for accelerating climate action in the coming years. Beşiktaş remains committed to advancing ambitious climate goals while contributing to global sustainability efforts.

La comuna de Punta Arenas se distingue a nivel nacional por ser la segunda comuna en aprobar su Plan de Acción Comunal de Cambio Climático (PACCC), consolidándose como un referente en la planificación climática local. Este reconocimiento refleja el compromiso de la municipalidad con la mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático, así como la capacidad de articular la participación ciudadana, la planificación territorial y la coordinación interinstitucional.

Actualmente, la comuna se encuentra en la etapa de implementación del PACCC, avanzando en proyectos concretos de educación ambiental, eficiencia energética, gestión de residuos, arborización urbana, conservación de humedales y desarrollo de infraestructura resiliente, entre otros. Esta fase no solo permite ejecutar las medidas contempladas, sino también generar información clave sobre resultados, impactos y desafíos, la cual sirve de base para la actualización del instrumento.

En este contexto, Punta Arenas proyecta ser la primera comuna del país en actualizar su PACCC para el año 2025, incorporando los aprendizajes y análisis obtenidos durante este período de implementación. Esta actualización permitirá reforzar metas, priorizar acciones de mayor impacto, integrar nuevas oportunidades de financiamiento y alinearse con los lineamientos nacionales y regionales en materia climática, consolidando a la comuna como líder en acción climática local y en gobernanza ambiental.

col1_Further information: As in past years, it remains difficult for a jurisdiction our size to quantitatively assess our climate impact due to lack of accurate data. This is particularly true of vehicle emissions. \nThis makes it very difficult for us to quantify improvement trends over time, in line with CDP and ICLEI's missions. This does not lend itself to the quantification responses CDP encourages, but nevertheless is the most effective way we have found to respond to the gathering crisis.

La Dirección Municipal de Medio Ambiente de Durango reafirma su compromiso con la acción climática y la sostenibilidad urbana. Como respaldo a este cuestionario, se anexa el Plan Anual de Trabajo 2025, que integra programas y acciones estratégicas en materia de:

Mitigación y adaptación al cambio climático, incluyendo la actualización del Programa Municipal de Cambio Climático y el fortalecimiento de capacidades técnicas para su implementación.

Gestión integral de residuos sólidos, con enfoque en la reducción, separación en origen y promoción del esquema “Basura Cero”.

Conservación y reforestación urbana, mediante la protección del arbolado, la ampliación de áreas verdes y la participación en iniciativas internacionales como Tree Cities of the World.

Educación y cultura ambiental, a través de programas comunitarios y escolares como Ecoguardianes, con el fin de sensibilizar a la ciudadanía en torno a la resiliencia climática.

Colaboración institucional, destacando la coordinación con dependencias municipales, estatales y federales, así como con organizaciones de la sociedad civil y el sector privado.

Con estas acciones, el municipio de Durango busca fortalecer su resiliencia climática, contribuir al cumplimiento de la Agenda 2030 y los ODS, y posicionarse como referente en transparencia ambiental al participar activamente en el CDP.

Catbalogan City is a developing city that continues to pursue urbanization while giving equal importance to protecting its natural environment and improving the wellbeing of its people. As the capital of Samar, it plays a central role in regional governance and economic activity, yet it remains highly dependent on its rich ecological resources, including its forests, coastal ecosystems, and agricultural lands. The city is located along Maqueda Bay and forms part of the Samar Island Natural Park, which places it within an area of both great biodiversity and high climate vulnerability. This unique position drives the city government to prioritize sustainable and inclusive approaches in planning and development.

The city's development direction is guided by a vision of becoming sustainable and resilient while ensuring that economic growth does not come at the expense of its ecosystems. Urbanization projects, such as improved housing and infrastructure through the Sky City program, are paired with strong environmental safeguards like the Forest Land Use Plan, the Urban Greening Plan, and the Local Energy Efficiency and Conservation Plan. In this way, Catbalogan seeks to maintain balance: creating opportunities for jobs, investment, and education while protecting forests, watersheds, mangroves, and marine resources that are vital for both ecological stability and community livelihoods.

Catbalogan also gives importance to inclusive governance by engaging communities, civil society, and academic institutions in the design and implementation of climate and environmental programs. The city understands that adaptation and mitigation actions are only effective if they respond to the needs of the people, especially vulnerable groups such as coastal barangays, upland farmers, and the urban poor. Programs like the Food Security Plan and Solid Waste Management Plan are therefore designed not only as environmental strategies but also as social interventions that safeguard health, nutrition, and quality of life.

As climate risks intensify through sea level rise, stronger typhoons, and unpredictable rainfall, the city is working to strengthen its adaptive capacity. At the same time, it is pursuing opportunities for renewable energy, energy efficiency, and sustainable land use to reduce emissions and address energy poverty. By embedding climate considerations into development planning, Catbalogan City is positioning itself as a city that grows responsibly, ensuring that progress is shared equitably among its people while protecting the natural foundations that sustain life and livelihoods.

In doing so, Catbalogan City continues to move forward as a developing hub of governance, commerce, and education while staying true to its commitment of preserving its environment, maintaining balance between people and nature, and working toward a sustainable and resilient future for all.

Melalui RPJMD 2025-2029, Kota Pontianak mengarusutamakan ketahanan lingkungan, adaptasi perubahan iklim, dan pengelolaan sumber daya yang efisien sebagai fondasi pembangunan jangka menengah. Komitmen ini diperkuat dengan integrasi isu perubahan iklim ke dalam strategi pembangunan lintas sektor—mulai dari penataan ruang, infrastruktur hijau, pelayanan publik, hingga transformasi digital—sehingga seluruh perangkat daerah memiliki peran yang jelas dalam menjaga keberlanjutan lingkungan dan meningkatkan kualitas hidup masyarakat.\n\nMelalui dokumen Rencana Aksi Iklim, Pontianak membangun pendekatan ilmiah dan kolaboratif untuk memperkuat ketahanan kota terhadap risiko iklim. Inventarisasi gas rumah kaca, pemetaan kerentanan kelurahan, serta rencana aksi mitigasi dan adaptasi dirumuskan secara komprehensif untuk memastikan bahwa pertumbuhan kota berjalan sejalan dengan upaya penurunan emisi dan peningkatan resilien masyarakat. Kolaborasi dengan akademisi, komunitas, dan mitra internasional memperkuat Pontianak sebagai kota percontohan aksi iklim di tingkat nasional dan regional, sekaligus memastikan bahwa keberlanjutan bukan sekadar slogan, tetapi praktik nyata yang terukur dan berorientasi pada masa depan warga kota.

Addressing climate change, a global issue, and contributing to national efforts at the local level through the development of plans and strategies related to climate change is of great importance. Reducing greenhouse gas emissions through the implementation of actions outlined in these plans, in line with national targets, will not only be a local effort but will also support the reduction of Turkey's total greenhouse gas emissions.

With the plan in place, we aim to reduce Kocaeli's greenhouse gas emissions by 41% by 2030, contributing to the nation's climate change efforts. We are committed to being a city that actively participates in all kinds of activities, applications, and studies that can be carried out with an effective and coordinated approach with all our stakeholders in order to achieve this goal.

By raising public environmental awareness, carrying out studies on what needs to be done to combat climate change, and providing environmental services in line with the needs of the people within a certain framework, we aim to make Kocaeli a model 'Climate Resilient and Adaptive City' that combats climate change in a planned manner and in accordance with international methodologies. The answers given to this survey and your valuable feedback will play a significant role in ensuring the sustainable growth of Kocaeli.

col1_Further information:
Iztapa está dando pasos agigantados en la acción climática, y para muestra uno de estos proyectos que esta en fase de consolidar los documentos que se necesitan. 
3.	Antecedentes del proyecto:

La región costera del Pacífico guatemalteco, se sustenta en actividades clave como la agroindustria, la pesca y el turismo. Los ecosistemas marino-costeros incluyen bosques de manglares y playas, hábitat de tortugas marinas, especies emblemáticas de valor tanto ecológico como económico, especialmente en el ámbito turístico.

Las comunidades locales dependen fuertemente de ecosistemas saludables, siendo los manglares fundamentales para su resiliencia ante eventos climáticos extremos y como fuentes de alimentos. No obstante, la contaminación por descargas domésticas e industriales y desechos sólidos, incluyendo las redes de pesca abandonadas, y los impactos crecientes de eventos climáticos extremos, agravados por la degradación de los manglares, amenazan la fauna, la salud humana y los medios de vida en la región.

Las prácticas generalizadas en la mayor parte de municipios en Guatemala de tirar, quemar o enterrar residuos sólidos sin ningún tratamiento agrava la situación de salud y ambiental que actualmente existe. De esta cuenta, se hace necesario llevar a cabo estudios de caracterización de residuos y desechos sólidos comunes, como la herramienta de información primaria que permita determinar la generación/habitante/día y generar datos comparables entre diferentes municipios. 

En Guatemala, el código municipal, Decreto 12-2002 y sus reformas, en su artículo 68 inciso a), indica que corresponde a las municipalidades la recolección, tratamiento y disposición final de desechos y residuos sólidos, así como regular y prestar los servicios públicos municipales en el territorio. 

Iztapa, es un municipio costero del departamento de Escuintla, ubicado en la costa del Pacífico guatemalteco. Se extiende sobre una superficie aproximada de 328 km² y está delimitado al norte por Guanagazapa, al este por Taxisco (Santa Rosa), al oeste por Masagua y Puerto San José, y al sur bañado por el Océano Pacífico. El municipio demanda soluciones sostenibles y locales para el manejo de sus desechos sólidos. Esto hace especialmente pertinente la implementación de un centro de segregación y transferencia de residuos, con el objetivo de mejorar la separación, aumentar la eficiencia operativa y reducir el impacto ambiental, en línea con una visión integrada de desarrollo sostenible.

El proyecto “Conservación de Ecosistemas Costeros para un Futuro Sostenible en la Costa del Pacífico de Guatemala” de WWF, se centra en la protección y revitalización de las funciones de estos ecosistemas. Aborda desafíos cruciales como la contaminación por plásticos, la gestión de residuos sólidos y la preservación de las tortugas marinas, promoviendo un desarrollo sostenible. Se implementará en colaboración estrecha con autoridades municipales, pescadores, comunidades, sector privado, MARN, INAB y CONAP.

4.	Objetivo general de la consultoría:

Contribuir de forma participativa al manejo integrado de la gestión de los residuos sólidos comunes del municipio de Iztapa, Escuintla, mediante el diseño, construcción y puesta en marcha de un centro de segregación y transferencia que cumpla con la normativa legal y ambiental vigente en Guatemala.

5.	Objetivos específicos:
1.	Diseñar el centro de segregación y transferencia de residuos sólidos, asegurando el cumplimiento de los requerimientos legales vigentes, y tramitar los permisos legales ante el MARN y el Ministerio de Salud Pública y Asistencia Social.
2.	Construir el centro en cumplimiento de las normas establecidas en el artículo 20 del Reglamento 164-2021 del MARN, incluyendo las obras y el equipamiento necesarios.
3.	Elaborar, de forma participativa, una propuesta de funcionamiento operativo y administrativo del centro, incluyendo el análisis de las diferentes opciones para su operativización (concesión, convenio con gestores de residuos, contratación de servicios externos, municipalidad u otras alternativas).

Bhavnagar Climate Resilient City Action Plan (CRCAP) has been prepared using ICLEI South Asia's ClimateResilientCities methodology. For this, ICLEI South Asia provided technical assistance to Bhavnagar Municipal Corporation for preparing the plan in line with the national, state and city government priorities, following GCoM's Common Reporting Framework (CRF). 

This action plan includes a detailed urban system gap analysis; climate risk and vulnerability assessment; a Global Protocol for Community-Scale Greenhouse Gas Emission (GPC) complaint GHG emissions inventory (2022-23); future emissions scenario modelling including Business-As-Usual projections (2025, 2027, 2030, 2040, 2050) and GHG emissions reduction scenario (Low Emission Growth Scenario for 2025, 2027, 2030).

The action plan encompasses 17 strategies and 83 actions across eight key urban sectors: 1) built environment and energy, 2) transport, 3) water, 4) wastewater, 5) storm water, 6) solid waste, 7) urban greening and biodiversity, and 8) air quality.

By implementing the measures specified in the Low Emissions Growth Scenario, Bhavnagar is positioned to reduce its GHG emissions by up to 16.3% compared to the business-as-usual (BAU) scenario by 2030.

The approval letter from the Bhavnagar Municipal Corporation's General Board (Council Approval) for the Climate Resilient City Action Plan (CRCAP), in native Gujarati language, has been attached for reference.

The CRCAP was initially approved by the Municipal Commissioner and subsequently forwarded to the Standing Committee of the Municipal Corporation, which granted its approval. Thereafter, the plan was placed before the General Board (Council) of the Corporation, where it received final approval.

Accordingly, the Climate Resilient City Action Plan has been formally approved and adopted by the city.

The Municipality of Del Carmen, Siargao Island, is a 5th-class coastal municipality globally recognized for its 4,871-hectare mangrove forest, designated in 2024 as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance.

Guided by the Local Climate Change Action Plan (LCCAP) 2024-2030, the LGU integrates ecosystem-based adaptation, sustainable tourism, and community-driven livelihood programs into its planning and budgeting.

Key priorities include mangrove rehabilitation and protection, renewable energy adoption (solar streetlighting and hybrid systems for public facilities), disaster risk reduction, and sustainable fisheries management.

To advance these priorities, the LGU actively proposes projects to national agencies and development partners such as DENR, DOT, and international donors—for example, sustainable ecotourism facilities, community-based mangrove conservation programs, and climate-resilient livelihood initiatives.

Del Carmen collaborates with provincial and regional agencies, national government programs, local fisherfolk associations, academic institutions, and civil society groups to scale up climate action, safeguard biodiversity, and strengthen community resilience in line with its Ramsar obligations.

The City of Nanaimo is somewhat unique in developing and monitoring sustainability policy. As noted in previous answers, Nanaimo was the first City in North America to endorse the Doughnut Economics model as the City's guiding framework. Doughnut economics provides a framework for sustainable development, ensuring that those in need are cared for, the environment is protected and business can flourish — while making the city livable for all. The “doughnut” consists of two concentric rings. The first ring is the social foundation, as defined by the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals, to ensure no one falls short on life's essentials. The second ring is the environmental ceiling, as determined by credible scientists, to ensure that humanity does not exceed the natural boundaries that protect Earth's life-supporting systems. The hole in the middle of the doughnut is where those lacking the basic requirements of life reside.

This concept framed the development of City Plan, Nanaimo's key policy document which included the Official Community Plan, Transportation Master Plan, Parks Master Plan and both the Climate Action Plan and Climate Change Resiliency Strategy into one document. The adoption of City Plan in 2022, was followed by Council's endorsement of the Integrated Action Plan in 2023 which prioritizes actions necessary to implement City Plan goals and policies; and finally, by the Monitoring Strategy in 2024, which monitors the City's progress towards ensuring the City is living within the inner boundary of the Doughnut Economic framework. The monitoring strategy itself uses a unique framework, known as the Multi-Capital Scorecard. The monitoring strategy monitors a number of areas of impact, including many related to climate change and sustainability. The strategy includes both 'key indicators' which tell us tell us how the City is doing at a high-level and how close or
how far we are to defined goals or aspirations and 'supportive indicators' tell us how the City is doing in a specific area and can
show us over time if we are moving in the right direction. While supportive indicators include traditional targets, for key indicators targets are replaced with 'sustainability end goals' which are 'quantified science- or ethics-based goals or aspirations that take into account environmental limits and a basic standard of wellbeing that all
residents have a claim of achieving'. During the CDP reporting we included both indicator types related to key sustainability impacts as well as progress on key actions. We realize the unique structure of Nanaimo's monitoring strategy may not translate well into the CDP reporting framework. We feel Nanaimo's policy, action and monitoring strategy is an effective way to achieve our sustainability goals. Nanaimo City Plan, including the Integrated Action Plan and Monitoring Strategy recently received a award of excellence in Sustainability from the Union of British Columbia municipalities. The Monitoring strategy is now complete and can be found here:
https://www.nanaimo.ca/property-development/sustainability/the-monitoring-strategy

Fortalezas de la JIAN
Modelo de gobernanza intermunicipal reconocido por el Estado, que coordina a 8 municipios de Altos Norte.

Cobertura territorial amplia (8,554 km², 10.8% de Jalisco), lo que le da peso estratégico en políticas regionales.

Capacidad técnica instalada: viveros forestales activos en San Diego y Villa Hidalgo, brigadas de restauración, humedales artificiales en operación.

Diversificación de acciones ambientales: cambio climático, agua, residuos, biodiversidad, cultura ambiental, manejo del fuego.

Experiencia en restauración y adaptación: con base en los árboles plantados, reúso de agua en humedales, ganadería regenerativa.

Articulación con academia y sociedad civil: convenios con universidades (UdeG, UNIVA, U. Querétaro, CIESAS), Club Rotario, asociaciones y productores.

Relaciones con sector privado y cooperación internacional: apoyo de empresas (DIAGEO, Reyma), participación en COBIOCOM, presencia en foros internacionales (UCO - Colombia).

Transparencia y rendición de cuentas: auditorías externas, sesiones de Junta de Gobierno, participación ciudadana incipiente.

Monitoreo y conservación de especies emblemáticas (Águila Real, aves migratorias), que generan visibilidad e interés global.

Capacidad de comunicación social: presencia en medios, blog institucional, ferias y festivales culturales.

Oportunidades para la JIAN
Acceso a financiamiento climático internacional gracias a su modelo intermunicipal y sus reportes de cambio climático.

Consolidación de una estrategia de economía circular (caravana al reciclaje, compostaje, acopio de electrónicos) con potencial de escalar regionalmente.

Desarrollo de proyectos productivos sostenibles (ej. floricultura en humedales, ganadería regenerativa, aprovechamiento de residuos).

Expansión de áreas de conservación voluntaria (ADVC) y corredores biológicos.

Fortalecer el vínculo con municipios en transición política (presidentes electos) para asegurar continuidad institucional.

Innovación tecnológica en gestión de recursos hídricos (captación de lluvia, monitoreo de calidad de agua, humedales multifuncionales).

Ampliar educación ambiental formal en escuelas, con programas regionales vinculados a ODS y cambio climático.

Posicionarse como referente regional en adaptación al cambio climático en zonas semiáridas, articulando experiencias con otras Juntas (JIRA, JINOR, etc.).

A iniciativa “Caminho Sustentável: Transformando o Bairro Novo Passo com Multiplicadores Ambientais”, no município de Cruzeiro do Sul (RS), surge como resposta à catástrofe climática de maio de 2024, que resultou na destruição do bairro Passo de Estrela. 
Seu objetivo é requalificar uma área de risco por meio de soluções sustentáveis e integradas, promovendo adaptação climática e reconstrução urbana segura, inclusiva e resiliente. A proposta envolve a criação de um parque linear multifuncional de 250.000 m², estruturado com Soluções baseadas na Natureza (SbN), e o desenvolvimento do bairro planejado Novo Passo, com área de 335.695 m², destinado ao reassentamento de famílias afetadas.
Mais de 300 famílias serão diretamente beneficiadas, com impacto indireto sobre diversas áreas urbanas vulneráveis de Cruzeiro do Sul. As ações incluem drenagem sustentável, arborização, educação ambiental e capacitação de multiplicadores ambientais locais. A iniciativa baseia-se no zoneamento de risco do Plano Diretor Municipal e articula-se com políticas públicas de habitação, urbanismo, meio ambiente e defesa civil.
Diferenciais do projeto incluem: articulação inédita entre requalificação ambiental e habitação digna; uso prioritário de infraestruturas baseadas na natureza; transformação de território vulnerável em espaço de convivência e preservação; inspiração nos princípios de cidade resiliente; e potencial de replicação em outros municípios impactados por eventos extremos.

As Üsküdar Municipality, we have adopted the “Vision Üsküdar” approach, a comprehensive strategic planning process in line with our district's 2050 vision. Within this framework, we reflect the foundations we lay today with the goal of a sustainable future in our daily policies and investments.
With the Vision Üsküdar approach, we ensure the effective and efficient use of resources with a holistic perspective that integrates all critical areas such as urban transformation, environmental management, social policy, and technology. In this way, we aim to support economic development while preserving ecological balance and social welfare.
In line with the goal of a disaster-resilient city, we are establishing the “Üsküdar is Renewing Platform” and making the urban transformation process economically sustainable. We are working to empower disadvantaged groups that are most affected during times of crisis. Accordingly, the Üsküdar Municipality Disaster Management Directorate was established in 2025.
 Under the coordination of the “Üsküdar Renewal Platform” and the Disaster Management Department, work is planned on many issues, such as disaster risk management and early warning systems, green infrastructure and natural solutions, energy efficiency and renewable energy use, sustainability in urban transformation, and reducing the carbon footprint. Thus, the goal is for our district to achieve a climate-resilient and sustainable structure.
We view education, technology, and entrepreneurship support for disadvantaged youth and women not as social assistance, but as fundamental tools for social and sustainable development. With this approach, we aim to increase economic independence and social resilience rather than alleviating poverty with temporary support. In addition, the number of female employees within our municipality has tripled.
Üsküdar occupies an important position with its rich historical heritage, and the district has many cultural heritage elements of different types, such as the Maiden's Tower, tekkes, statues, fountains, mosques, tombs, and pavilions. Among these structures, there are 975 registered historical buildings, and there are also thousands of unregistered historical buildings in the district.
Due to the density of historical structures and its tourist appeal, Üsküdar is an important destination. Istanbul hosts a record number of tourists during the summer months, welcoming a total of 5,345,835 tourists in June, July, and August 2024. This density is also reflected in Üsküdar.
Our analysis based on TÜİK data shows that 10-20% of tourists visiting Istanbul during the summer months visit Üsküdar, and according to this, the estimated number of visitors to Üsküdar is around 1,069,167 people. At this point, the protection of historical heritage comes to the fore among the measures to be taken against the climate crisis. 
Üsküdar attracts attention not only with its historical and cultural heritage but also with its natural riches. The monumental trees within the district boundaries represent a living heritage that has survived from the past to the present day, preserving the city's ecological memory. Furthermore, bird watching spots and natural habitats along the coastline provide opportunities for both the preservation of biological diversity and the integration of city residents with nature. In this context, as Üsküdar Municipality, we are determinedly continuing our efforts to strengthen green infrastructure, protect natural resources, and pass them on to future generations.

Quảng Bình Province is deeply committed to advancing its climate resilience and sustainability goals, ensuring that our strategies are fully aligned with Vietnam's National Climate Change Strategy to 2050, as well as key international frameworks such as the Paris Agreement and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As a coastal province in central Vietnam, Quảng Bình faces significant vulnerabilities to climate change impacts, including frequent typhoons, heavy rainfall leading to flash floods, riverine and urban flooding, drought, saline intrusion, coastal erosion, and rising sea levels. These hazards not only threaten our natural ecosystems—such as the UNESCO-listed Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park and extensive mangrove forests—but also impact the livelihoods of our 924,757 residents (as of 2024), particularly in rural and coastal communities where agriculture, fisheries, and tourism are primary economic drivers. In response, our CDP submission highlights a holistic approach that integrates nature-based solutions (NbS), resilient infrastructure development, and robust community engagement into all aspects of provincial planning, budgeting, and implementation.

Our governance structures reflect a strong emphasis on climate oversight, with the Provincial People's Committee (PPC) leading the charge through dedicated committees, management-level responsibilities, and integration of climate considerations into performance objectives, risk management policies, and major capital expenditures. For instance, we have established Provincial Project Management Units (PPMUs) to coordinate with departments like Agriculture and Environment, ensuring that climate-related issues inform everything from socio-economic master plans to sectoral strategies in agriculture, water resources, forestry, and urban development. This institutional framework has enabled us to develop and implement key initiatives, such as the Provincial Climate Change Action Response Plan for 2025-2030 with a vision to 2050, which builds on national directives like Decision No. 896/QD-TTg and incorporates projects under the VN-SIPA II program supported by GIZ and the International Climate Initiative (IKI).

Recent collaborations have been pivotal in translating these plans into tangible actions. Partnerships with international organizations such as the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the Green Climate Fund (GCF), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), and the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) have facilitated pilot projects that demonstrate innovative approaches to adaptation and mitigation. Notable examples include the construction of climate-resilient housing for poor and near-poor households in coastal districts, featuring flood-proof designs like raised mezzanines and reinforced roofing, which have already benefited hundreds of families and reduced disaster recovery costs. In urban areas, such as Đồng Hới City, we are advancing ecosystem-based adaptation through sustainable drainage systems, green infrastructure, and flood management initiatives funded under ADB's Urban Environment and Climate Change Adaptation Project. Additionally, nature-based solutions in communes like Tuyên Hóa, Bố Trạch, and Minh Hóa are promoting climate-smart agriculture, community-based forest management, and mangrove restoration, enhancing biodiversity while providing natural buffers against storms and erosion.

On the mitigation front, Quảng Bình is positioning itself as a renewable energy hub in Vietnam's central region. Our Provincial Master Plan for 2021-2030, with a vision to 2050, targets over 6,000 MW of renewable capacity by mid-century, dominated by wind and solar power. Current progress includes operational solar plants contributing around 380 MW, with ambitious proposals like Vingroup's 3,000 MW nearshore wind project underway, which could attract up to USD 3.9 billion in investment and significantly reduce greenhouse gas emissions. These efforts align with national targets for methane reduction in livestock and overall emissions cuts, while fostering green jobs and economic diversification.

Despite these advancements, Quảng Bình acknowledges ongoing challenges that require continued attention. Securing sustained financing remains a key hurdle, as many projects rely on external ODA and grants, with provincial budgets stretched across competing priorities. Enhancing institutional capacity for monitoring, evaluation, and data-driven decision-making is another area of focus, particularly in developing robust M&E systems for river basin monitoring, emissions inventories, and vulnerability assessments. We are also committed to ensuring equitable distribution of benefits, with disaggregated data collection on gender, poverty, and geographic vulnerability guiding our actions to support frontline communities, ethnic minorities, and low-income groups.

Looking ahead, Quảng Bình welcomes further partnerships and investments to scale up these initiatives. Opportunities abound in renewable energy expansion, including offshore wind surveys and grid integration; resilient infrastructure projects like urban drainage and reservoir safety rehabilitation; and community-driven adaptation models that incorporate indigenous knowledge and social equity. By fostering collaborations with national ministries, international donors, private sector investors, NGOs, and academia, we aim to accelerate our transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient economy. This CDP submission not only reflects our ongoing efforts but also serves as a call to action for collective progress, ensuring that Quảng Bình contributes meaningfully to Vietnam's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) while building a prosperous, inclusive future for all residents. We are grateful for the CDP platform in amplifying our voice and facilitating global knowledge exchange.

Known as the land of the ancient capital with a rich cultural heritage, Thua Thien Hue is also one of the localities most severely impacted by climate change. However, rather than remaining passive, Thua Thien Hue has emerged as a bright spot and one of the leading provinces in Vietnam in addressing and adapting to climate change. In addition to the efforts previously mentioned in this Questionnaire, other notable efforts by Thua Thien Hue include:

Implementation of the Paris Agreement Action Plan (2020)
•	The Provincial People's Committee officially issued the Action Plan to implement the Paris Agreement in Thua Thien Hue under Decision No. 3283/QD-UBND dated December 25, 2020.
•	This plan aligns with the spirit of Decision No. 2053/QD-TTg by the Prime Minister, aiming to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, promote green growth, and enhance adaptation capacity.
•	Key tasks include: 
o	GHG Emission Reduction: Conducting periodic provincial GHG inventories, developing renewable energy (solar power on the Tam Giang - Cau Hai Lagoon, efficient lighting NAMA, LNG), and promoting afforestation and forest protection.
o	Adaptation: Developing climate change scenarios, protecting coastal heritage sites, addressing river and coastal erosion, developing flood drainage infrastructure, upgrading reservoirs and the Thao Long Dam, establishing flood warning systems, and planting coastal and mangrove forests.
o	Resource Preparation: Training officials to implement the Paris Agreement, enhancing healthcare capacity to respond to natural disasters, and piloting new climate-adaptive technologies.
o	MRV System (Measurement, Reporting, Verification): Establishing a provincial system for monitoring, reporting, and verifying GHG emission reductions and adaptation efforts.

Development of Climate-Resilient Agriculture
•	Promoting High-Tech and Sustainable Agriculture: 
o	The city has implemented programs to restructure agriculture toward sustainability and climate change adaptation, focusing on: 
-	Developing high-tech agriculture, organic farming, and production models adhering to VietGap standards.
-	Supporting large-scale field models through land consolidation, applying advanced scientific techniques, and developing biosafe livestock farming.
o	Outcomes: Increased agricultural productivity and quality, enhanced resilience to harsh climate conditions such as droughts and floods, and contributions to ensuring food security.
Urban Planning and Sustainable Development
•	Raising the Elevation of Roads and Buildings: 
o	The city authorities have prioritized elevating major roads and construction sites, particularly in low-lying areas, to ensure accessibility during floods and reduce the impact of flooding on residential areas.
o	Outcomes: Urban areas such as Phu Binh, Phu Hoi, and newly developed wards experience reduced flooding impacts, improving accessibility and safety for residents.
•	Integrating Drainage Systems into New Projects: 
o	New urban and infrastructure projects are required to include drainage systems connected to the city's overall network, ensuring no localized flooding or exacerbation of flooding in surrounding areas.
o	Outcomes: More sustainable urban development, with reduced flood risks in newly expanded areas like An Van Duong.
•	Land Use and Zoning Control: 
o	The city has implemented measures to regulate urban expansion to protect natural lakes, ponds, and green spaces, which play a critical role in water retention and natural drainage.
o	Outcomes: Preservation of natural ecosystems like the Tam Giang - Cau Hai Lagoon, contributing to reduced flood risks and the maintenance of biodiversity.

Raising Community Awareness and Education
•	Public Awareness Campaigns on Drainage and Environmental Protection: 
o	The city has launched local communication campaigns to raise public awareness about waste management, preventing littering in canals, lakes, and natural waterways. This helps reduce drainage system blockages and maintain clear water flow.
o	Outcomes: Reduced clogging of drainage systems, improved drainage efficiency, and increased community participation in climate change adaptation efforts.
•	Collaboration with International Organizations: 
o	Hue City has partnered with organizations such as JICA, the World Bank, and the Asian Development Bank to implement climate change response projects. These projects provide not only financial resources but also technology transfer and knowledge sharing.
o	Outcomes: Enhanced local technical and managerial capacity to address climate challenges, thereby improving the effectiveness of adaptation and mitigation measures.

Contributions to National and International Goals
•	Participation in International Agreements: 
o	Through central government programs, Hue City has contributed to the goals of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Protocol, and the Paris Agreement. Activities include: 
	Implementing Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions (NAMA).
	Committing to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, with a target increase from 8% to 25% with international support.
o	Outcomes: Contributed to national efforts to keep global temperature rise below 2°C compared to pre-industrial levels, while elevating the city's standing in global initiatives.
•	National Climate Change Strategy: 
o	The city has actively integrated disaster risk management and climate change adaptation into 90% of its socio-economic development plans, including initiatives for green urban development and sustainable industrial spaces.
o	Outcomes: Enhanced resilience to climate change, reduced disaster risks, and promotion of sustainable development toward a low-carbon economy.

Lügde, a small but forward-looking city in the Kreis Lippe, has made significant strides in both climate protection (mitigation) and climate change adaptation, embracing a holistic approach across multiple sectors. Central to its efforts is a strong political and administrative commitment to decarbonization, energy efficiency, and sustainability, demonstrated by concrete projects, institutional structures, and forward-looking strategies.

Institutional and Strategic Foundations

To coordinate its climate actions, Lügde established a climate-protection manager (Klimaschutzmanager) position on 1 June 2021, funded partly through the German Federal Government's National Climate Initiative. 
luegde.de
 This role is tasked with implementing the city's climate protection concept and turning strategic ambitions into real measures. 
luegde.de
+1

Lügde's climate efforts are embedded in the broader Masterplan 100 % Klimaschutz of the Kreis Lippe, a region-wide roadmap developed in close collaboration with all 16 municipalities, local energy providers, businesses, and civil society. 
Klimaschutz
+1
 This inter-municipal coordination helps maximize synergies and avoid duplication, reinforcing Lügde's capacity to make a meaningful contribution to regional climate goals.

At the district level, the integrated climate strategy called “Lippe_Re-Klimatisiert” (LiReK) has played a central role. 
Kreis Lippe
 This program combined 15 concrete measures in the domains of buildings, mobility, and behavioral change, backed by substantial funding (about 20 million €), mostly from EU regional development funds and state funds. 
Kreis Lippe
+1
 When LiReK concluded in 2023, it had already achieved estimated annual savings of 3,900 tons of CO₂ across its projects. 
Kreis Lippe

Wind Energy and Renewable Power

Lügde's commitment to renewable energy is particularly evident in its wind energy projects. The city has approved and permitted multiple wind turbines in its outer areas. 
Kreis Lippe
+1
 For example, in 2024 the Kreis Lippe granted approval for two large Enercon E-160 turbines (each with a nominal capacity of 5.56 MW) in Lügde. 
Kreis Lippe

Moreover, a prominent repowering project is underway in the WindStrom Niese-Köterberg wind park, north of Niese (part of Lügde). In this initiative, nine old wind turbines are being replaced by three modern, high-capacity machines with a total output of 13.5 MW—sufficient to supply more than 11,000 two-person households. 
WindStrom Niese-Köterberg
 This reflects Lügde's clear will to increase renewable generation, improve efficiency, and phase out outdated fossil-heavy or inefficient infrastructure.

Together, these efforts contribute strongly to the decarbonization of Lügde's energy supply and reduce dependence on fossil fuels, showing that the city is not only embracing renewables but doing so in a smart, long-term, and scalable way.

Energy Management and Efficiency

Beyond producing green power, Lügde is also focusing on energy efficiency and management. The climate-protection office promotes municipal energy management, including in city-owned buildings, public infrastructure, and services. 
luegde.de
+1
 The city participates in regional energy networks (e.g., via KlimaPakt Lippe) to coordinate its efforts, share best practices, and benefit from advice, investments, and public-private partnerships. 
luegde.de
+2
klimapakt-lippe.de
+2

In its buildings, Lügde supports energy-saving renovation: through its participation in the KlimaPakt Lippe, citizens and local businesses can access energy advice, funding, and expert support for thermal refurbishment, better insulation, efficient heating systems, and solar installations. 
luegde.de
 This contributes to reducing the city's carbon footprint while also saving money and improving residents' quality of life.

Flood Protection and Heavy Rain Preparedness

Recognizing that climate change brings not only gradual warming but more frequent extreme weather, Lügde has proactively addressed flood risk and heavy-rain (Starkregen) risk. In 2024, the city received a grant of €31,700 from the regional government to develop a Starkregen-risk management concept. 
Lippische Landes-Zeitung
 This concept will map potential flood zones, identify vulnerable buildings and institutions (e.g., schools, senior homes), and recommend technical and planning measures to prevent or mitigate flash flooding. 
Lippische Landes-Zeitung

At the broader district level, the Klimaschutzteilkonzept Anpassung (climate-adaptation sub-concept) elaborated by Lippe includes flood retention, natural stream restoration, and planning tools such as risk maps and local flood-hazard mapping. 
Kreis Lippe
 These kinds of nature-based solutions help slow down runoff, create retention areas, and reduce the risk of damage during extreme rainfall.

Through these adaptation measures, Lügde shows that it takes climate resilience seriously: preparing for more volatile precipitation, protecting its infrastructure, and safeguarding its citizens.

Decarbonizing Industry and Efficiency

While Lügde is not a large industrial metropolis, its climate strategy explicitly emphasizes a strong willingness to decarbonize wherever possible, including in industry and commerce. Through its network with the KlimaPakt Lippe, the city engages local companies in energy- and climate-friendly transitions. 
luegde.de
+1
 The KlimaPakt offers platforms for businesses to innovate, share best practices, and adopt efficiency-increasing technologies, renewable energy, and CO₂ reduction strategies.

Moreover, through the Masterplan 100% Klimaschutz, Lügde aligns with regional ambitions to support a post-fossil economy. 
Klimaschutz
 The city fosters a culture in which sustainable industrial development is not just desirable, but feasible: combining climate ambition with economic viability, and encouraging companies to invest in low-carbon technologies, energy reuse, and smarter processes.

Forest and Natural Landscape Development

In addition to its energy and built-environment efforts, Lügde has a strong commitment to natural climate assets. The region includes important forest landscapes and protected natural areas, such as parts of the Schwalenberger Wald within the district's boundaries. 
Wikipedia
 These forests not only serve biodiversity, but also act as carbon sinks, helping sequester CO₂ over time and contributing to climate mitigation.

Lügde and the Kreis Lippe also promote ecological development and preservation of natural areas, including stream restoration, river bank renaturation, and green corridor planning, in line with adaptation strategies. 
Kreis Lippe
 Protected nature reserves such as the Ilsenbach Valley (Naturschutzgebiet Ilsenbach) underscore the city's dedication to preserving and enhancing natural habitats. 
Wikipedia

By focusing on forest development, restoration, and the protection of natural ecosystems, Lügde integrates biodiversity, carbon storage, and risk management in a coherent climate strategy.

Public Engagement, Behavior Change, and Partnerships

Lügde's climate success also draws on public participation and effective partnerships. Through the KlimaPakt Lippe, the city involves citizens, businesses, schools, and other stakeholders in a shared commitment to climate action. 
klimapakt-lippe.de
+1
 The KlimaPakt supports initiatives like energy advice, sustainable renovation, and knowledge exchange, making climate protection a collective effort.

Behavior change is also part of the strategy: for instance, in the LiReK program, gamification tools were used to motivate energy-saving behavior among municipal employees, encouraging lower consumption through a playful digital platform. 
Kreis Lippe

Ambition, Vision, and the Road Ahead

Taken together, Lügde's achievements reflect more than just small local projects. They embody a visionary will to decarbonize its energy systems, to raise energy efficiency across public and private sectors, and to prepare for the physical risks posed by climate change. By aligning energy production (wind), consumption (buildings, transport), and adaptation (flood, heavy rain, natural landscapes), Lügde demonstrates a systems thinking approach.

Moreover, its engagement in regional structures such as the Kreis Lippe's Masterplan and Lippe_Re-Klimatisiert ensures that local actions are amplified and reinforced by shared goals. The support for heavy-rain risk management and flood resilience shows a realistic acknowledgment that climate change is already having effects—and that adaptation is as important as mitigation.

In its forest and nature efforts, Lügde recognizes the multi-faceted value of trees and ecosystems—not only for biodiversity, but also for carbon storage, water regulation, and climate resilience.

Finally, the city's willingness to decarbonize industrial and commercial actors, to scale up renewable energy (especially modern wind turbines), to improve energy management, and to engage its citizens underscores a deep, long-term commitment. Lügde is not just reacting to climate change; it is proactively shaping a low-carbon, resilient future.

O Município de Sinop encontra-se em um processo contínuo de fortalecimento de sua gestão ambiental e climática. Embora ainda esteja estruturando um plano climático formal, a cidade já desenvolve diversas ações que contribuem direta e indiretamente para a mitigação e adaptação aos impactos das mudanças climáticas.

Sinop possui importantes ativos ambientais, como o Parque Florestal, as Reservas R1, R2 e R3 e extensas áreas verdes distribuídas pela malha urbana. Esses espaços funcionam como reguladores climáticos naturais, auxiliam na redução de ilhas de calor e protegem nascentes e cursos d'água essenciais para o equilíbrio ecológico urbano.

A cidade também enfrenta desafios típicos de municípios com rápido crescimento populacional, como expansão urbana acelerada, pressão sobre áreas de preservação, pontos de alagamento e aumento da vulnerabilidade a queimadas e eventos extremos. Em contrapartida, o município realiza ações permanentes de fiscalização ambiental, prevenção de queimadas, manejo de resíduos, ampliação da arborização e melhorias de drenagem urbana, fortalecendo sua capacidade de adaptação climática.

Parcerias com instituições como a UFMT, órgãos estaduais e organizações ambientais têm contribuído para pesquisas, educação ambiental, desenvolvimento de projetos e fortalecimento das políticas públicas locais.

Por fim, o município tem potencial para avançar em projetos de energia renovável, monitoramento ambiental digital, soluções baseadas na natureza, revitalização de APPs urbanas, expansão de infraestrutura verde e elaboração de planos setoriais que subsidiem um futuro Plano Climático Municipal. The Island Garden City of Samal (IGaCoS) in Davao del Norte was nominated and later recognized as the Philippines' sole recipient of the 6th ASEAN Environmentally Sustainable Cities (ESC) Award 2025. This prestigious award highlights the city's excellence in Clean Air, Clean Water, Clean Land, Urban Biodiversity & Green Spaces, and Circular Economy.

Environmental Achievements

Waste Management
- Operational sanitary landfill & septage treatment facility.

- Strict enforcement of “No Segregation, No Collection” policy → 43.22% waste diversion rate (above the national 25% target).

- Ban on single-use plastics (aligned with RA 11898).

Marine & Coastal Protection
- 18 Marine Protected Areas (MPAs).

- Creative use of plastic waste bottles as sea barriers.

Sustainability Innovations

- Environmental User Fee (EUF) Program funds mangrove rehab, MPAs, and waste facilities.

- TrashCash PH (mobile platform incentivizing plastic collection).

- Pure Oceans partnership - plastic waste converted into construction materials.

Education & Community Engagement

- Strong implementation of CEPA (communication, education, and public awareness) campaigns.

Awards for environmental education (Gawad Galing Kamalayan).

- Frequent coastal clean-ups and school-based advocacy.

International Partnerships

- Collaborations with EU, UNDP, WWF, UNCDF.

- Candidate city for SMART ASEAN Green Cities Programme.

- Shortlisted by DENR for a €60M EU grant on circular economy and climate resilience.

Awards & Recognitions

- ASEAN ESC Award 2025 (Langkawi, Malaysia).

- DENR-EMB XI Environment Summit (Aug 2025) - Four major awards, including ASEAN Distinguished Award and recognition for landfill contribution, waste management, and circular economy initiatives.

- Water Forum 2025 - Plaque & certificate for Septage Treatment Facility and Septage Management Ordinance.

- PLLENRO National Convention 2024 - Awards for:

Coastal Resource Management (Gawad Galing Katubigan)

Solid Waste Management (Gawad Galing Kalinisan)

Environmental Education (Gawad Galing Kamalayan).

IGaCoS has emerged as a national and regional model of eco-governance. Its integrated approach, waste management, marine protection, innovative sustainability programs, and active community participation, has earned it prestigious ASEAN and national awards. The city is now benchmarked by other LGUs seeking to replicate its environmental strategies.

Key Achievements of Cà Mau Province in Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation
Below are the notable achievements of Cà Mau Province in addressing climate change (adaptation and mitigation):
1. Building Infrastructure for Disaster Prevention and Sustainable Adaptation
Construction of a 55.7 km Western Sea Dike: This robust dike system has been built to combat coastal erosion and protect the shoreline, laying the foundation for mangrove forest restoration and enhancing resilience against storms, storm surges, and sea-level rise.
Dikes and salinity control structures have protected approximately 123,058 ha of agricultural land in Ngọc Hiển and Năm Căn districts from saltwater intrusion.
The Western Sea Dike Project marks a milestone in efforts to strengthen erosion prevention and climate change adaptation.
2. Ecosystem Restoration — 'Nature-Based Solutions' and Emission Reduction
Restored over 4,000 ha of mangrove forests, contributing to climate change mitigation, biodiversity conservation, and the promotion of sustainable livelihoods.
3. Enhancing Disaster Warning and Forecasting Systems
Established early warning systems in 24 high-risk communes, enabling communities to proactively respond and minimize damage during natural disasters.
4. Establishing Planning, Raising Awareness, and Promoting Green Transformation
The Provincial Party Standing Committee issued a directive emphasizing:
Integration of proactive climate change response policies and resource protection.
Promotion of green transformation, circular economy, renewable energy, low-carbon economy, and sustainable development.
Competitions, educational activities, and communication campaigns on climate-resilient housing and salinity intrusion prevention have been organized, fostering collaboration between communities and authorities.
5. Research and Policy Development for Water Resource Management
2025 Scientific Conference: Focused on “integrated groundwater management for climate change adaptation,” proposing technology models, policies, and community-driven sustainable water management solutions.
Coastal adaptation projects in collaboration with GIZ, the World Bank, IUCN/SNV, and others, focusing on:
Construction of dikes and flood-prevention structures.
Restoration of mangrove forests integrated with shrimp farming under the forest canopy.
Improving livelihoods for coastal communities.

Kota Magelang merupakan kota kecil di Jawa Tengah dengan luas wilayah ±18,5 km² dan jumlah penduduk sekitar 121.000 jiwa. Sebagai kota dengan ruang terbatas dan topografi berbukit, Magelang menghadapi tantangan unik dalam adaptasi iklim seperti genangan, keterbatasan ruang terbuka hijau, serta ketergantungan pada sumber air mata air.

Meski memiliki keterbatasan fiskal dan sumber daya, Kota Magelang telah menunjukkan komitmen terhadap pembangunan berketahanan iklim melalui program Kampung Iklim (ProKlim), keterlibatan dalam inisiatif internasional Plastic Smart Cities bersama WWF, serta penguatan integrasi isu iklim ke dalam dokumen perencanaan seperti RPJMD, KLHS, dan RAD-GRK.

Aksi-aksi iklim di Kota Magelang banyak mengandalkan pendekatan berbasis komunitas dan kolaborasi lintas sektor, termasuk dengan pemerintah provinsi, kementerian, serta mitra non-pemerintah. Dukungan lebih lanjut untuk penguatan kapasitas teknis, data emisi yang terintegrasi, serta mekanisme pembiayaan hijau sangat penting untuk mempercepat transisi menuju kota rendah karbon dan tangguh iklim.

Kota Magelang siap menjadi percontohan untuk kota kecil yang tangguh dan berkomitmen terhadap aksi iklim berkelanjutan.

The following additional information provides relevant context to Phu Yen Province's climate change response, particularly for a CDP Cities, States and Regions (or similar) questionnaire:
Climate Change Vulnerability and Adaptation Focus
Phu Yen, as a south-central coastal province of Vietnam, is highly vulnerable to climate change impacts, which dictate its adaptation priorities:
•	Key Hazards: The province is highly susceptible to sea-level rise, heavy rainfall, and an increasing frequency and intensity of storms and tropical depressions. The inland areas also face issues like drought and unpredictable rainfall patterns.
•	Vulnerable Sectors/Communities: The local economy and livelihoods are directly threatened. Research in the region highlights specific vulnerabilities in agriculture (especially rice farming impacted by drought and floods), fisheries, and the livelihoods of rural/coastal communities due to the high exposure to natural disasters.
•	Adaptation Projects: The province is actively engaged in climate-resilient infrastructure development. This includes projects focused on:
o	Upgrading and constructing climate- and disaster-resilient transport infrastructure (roads).
o	Improving water resource infrastructure to ensure reliable supply for communities, especially in upland and ethnic minority areas.
o	Developing robust data systems for climate and disaster risk management to improve early warnings and forecasting capacity.
 Strategic Integration with Provincial Master Plan
Phu Yen's climate action is officially integrated into its long-term economic strategy, giving it significant policy weight:
•	Master Plan (2021-2030, Vision 2050): The approved provincial Master Plan mandates a shift towards a modern, sustainable, and blue economy growth model.
•	Pillars of Growth: The core economic pillars are designed to be climate-aligned, focusing on:
o	Industry and Green Energy (as previously discussed, with a focus on solar, wind, and green hydrogen/ammonia).
o	High-quality services and Green Tourism (tapping natural heritage while minimizing impact).
o	High-tech agriculture and maritime logistics.
•	National Alignment: The provincial strategy is a localized application of Vietnam's overarching national strategies, including the National Green Growth Strategy (2021-2030) and the National Strategy on Climate Change to 2050, ensuring a consistent policy framework for both mitigation and adaptation.
Mitigation Context: Renewable Energy and Grid Issues
While mitigation efforts are strong on the generation side, the challenge of delivering that clean energy remains a key context point for any CDP disclosure:
•	High Renewable Potential: The province has excellent potential for solar and wind generation, attracting significant investment.
•	Grid Constraint: A critical limiting factor is the existing grid congestion and limited transmission capacity. This has historically led to curtailment (wasting clean power) and is the main driver for Phu Yen's focus on Green Hydrogen/Ammonia production—a strategy that converts otherwise 'stranded' renewable electricity into an exportable, low-carbon product, effectively bypassing the domestic grid issue.

O município de São Lourenço do Sul, com população inferior a 50 mil habitantes e IDH alto (0,7-0,799), possui emissões per capita estimadas abaixo de 3 tCO2e. Reconhecendo sua vulnerabilidade às mudanças climáticas, especialmente a enchentes, estiagens, vendavais e elevação do nível da Lagoa dos Patos, o município aderiu ao Pacto Global de Prefeitos e ao ICLEI, iniciando a estruturação de um Plano Climático Integrado.

Foram identificados como grupos mais expostos a população rural, comunidades ribeirinhas, crianças e idosos, com setores críticos como agricultura, saúde, infraestrutura urbana e recursos hídricos. A proporção da população exposta a riscos climáticos é considerada significativa (30-40%).

Entre os principais fatores que desafiam a adaptação estão as limitações financeiras e técnicas, mas também há suporte por meio de parcerias com universidades, ICLEI, ONU-Habitat e redes de cidades resilientes.

O município já estabeleceu metas iniciais: ampliar a participação de energias renováveis no consumo público de 10% (2023) para 30% até 2030, avançar na reciclagem de resíduos sólidos, ampliar a mobilidade ativa e recuperar áreas degradadas. Essas metas estão alinhadas aos ODS e ao compromisso de reduzir emissões de GEE no médio e longo prazo.

O Plano Climático Integrado aborda mitigação (energia limpa, mobilidade sustentável, gestão de resíduos e agricultura de baixo carbono) e adaptação (defesa civil, infraestrutura verde, proteção hídrica e saúde preventiva). Cenários climáticos regionais e projeções do IPCC deram consistência às estratégias, priorizando riscos já recorrentes e projeções futuras.

Por fim, São Lourenço do Sul reforça sua governança climática com a criação de comitês intersetoriais, conferências municipais e mecanismos de monitoramento periódico, demonstrando comprometimento com a resiliência local e com as metas globais de enfrentamento da crise climática.

Obtencion de certificacion Iso 14001

La Municipalidad de San Borja refuerza la gestión y trabajo hacia el cuidado de nuestro medio ambiente.La Municipalidad con fecha 01 de julio recibió la certificación ISO: 14001-2015, en su Sistema de Gestión Ambiental. Este paso refleja el continuo esfuerzo y dedicación de la institución hacia la promoción del cuidado de nuestro planeta.

Nuestra trayectoria se ha caracterizado por la implementación de iniciativas innovadoras que promueven la sostenibilidad ambiental y el bienestar de nuestros vecinos y colaboradores. Gracias a proyectos como los biohuertos urbanos, la Casa de Energía Kallpa Wasi y las plantas de tratamiento del agua, hemos asegurado una mejora continua en la calidad de vida de nuestra comunidad.

La política establecida, refleja nuestro compromiso con la excelencia en la prestación de servicios públicos y la protección del medio ambiente, brindando servicios innovadores, sensibles y participativos que satisfagan las necesidades y expectativas de todas nuestras partes interesadas.

Conociendo San Borja 

El distrito de San Borja se encuentra ubicado en la zona sureste de la provincia de Lima. El distrito de San Borja cuenta con 113247 mil habitantes (INEI, 2017). San Borja cuenta con una superficie aproximada de 9,96 km2. 

El 13.5% de la superficie del distrito de San Borja está representado por áreas verdes de uso público, de las cuales los parques y las bermas centrales de avenidas son los espacios que poseen una mayor cobertura arbórea, caso contrario al de las bermas laterales de calles, jirones y avenidas del distrito. El distrito se ha dividido en 12 sectores que a su vez se han dividido en subsectores A, B y C. 

 La Municipalidad de San Borja ha ratificado su participación en el Pacto Global de Alcaldes por el Clima y la Energía1, por medio del cual, la Municipalidad se comprometió a implementar políticas y tomar medidas para reducir (o limitar cuando relevante) las emisiones de gases de efecto invernadero, prepararse para los impactos del cambio climático, aumentar acceso a energía sostenibles y el seguimiento del progreso hacia los objetivos.

Em 2016, o Município já detinha de ações setoriais que auxiliam o desenvolvimento e o fortalecimento de uma capacidade técnica, institucional e política que possibilita o amadurecimento e o avanço da cidade para a ação local ao combate à mudança climática como a Política Municipal de Resíduos Sólidos (Lei n.º 482/2016) e o Plano de Gestão Integrada de Resíduos Sólidos com atualização periódica alinhada ao Plano Plurianual. 
Em 2019, elaborou o Plano Municipal de Saneamento Básico, tendo como princípios fundamentais a universalização dos serviços de saneamento básico, para que todos tenham acesso ao abastecimento de água com qualidade e em quantidade suficientes às suas necessidades, à coleta e tratamento adequados do esgoto e dos resíduos sólidos, e ao manejo correto das águas pluviais, e o Plano de Mobilidade (PLANMOB), com propostas e diretrizes com ações de curto, médio e longo prazo, visando atender o disposto na Política Nacional de Mobilidade Urbana (Lei Federal n.º 12.587/12).
O compromisso público com a agenda de enfrentamento da crise climática vem direcionando esforços de Abaetetuba mais fortemente desde o início de 2021. Em 2023, Abaetetuba criou o Grupo de Trabalho de Ação Climática Municipal (Decreto Municipal n°. 180/2023) subsidiado pela Política Estadual sobre Mudanças Climáticas do Pará (Lei nº 9048, de 29 de abril de 2020), com o intuito de implementar estruturas institucionais a fim de assegurar a construção do processo de implementação o seu plano estratégico de ação climática. Em complemento, o município também passou, no mesmo ano, a adotar a Agenda 2030 para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) como diretriz de políticas públicas em âmbito municipal (Lei Municipal n.º 683/2023) e criou a Comissão Municipal para o Desenvolvimento Sustentável (Decreto Municipal n.º 193/2023), resultado da pactuação realizada pela gestão municipal a Coalização Estratégia ODS. 
Outras ações enquanto políticas públicas e projetos demostram que Abaetetuba já vem desenvolvendo um trabalho intersetorial e não está partindo do zero na atuação climática, dentre estas:
No setor de Energia, o Município passou, em 2022, a realizar a troca de luminárias antigas por lâmpadas de LED em todo o município. Essa iniciativa visa modernizar o parque de iluminação pública, reduzir gastos e aumentar a eficiência energética na cidade. 
No Setor de Transporte, o Município vem esforçando-se para melhorar toda sua infraestrutura viária, visando desde a implementação de transporte público coletivo a melhorias no sistema cicloviário propostos no Plano de Mobilidade (PANMOB, 2019).
No Setor de Resíduos, Abaetetuba implementou, em 2022, a rota da Coleta Seletiva, com o objetivo de melhorar as condições ambientais, e recupera 2,52% do total de resíduos coletados no município. No estado, a taxa de recuperação é de 0,5%, e no país é de 3,31% (SNIS, 2022).
